correctness.rationale: For each tree the integral incidence Gram determinant is n; each signed facet pyramid has volume sqrt(n)/(n-1)! and is at height 1/||h_s||, giving exact facet area sqrt(n)||h_s||/(n-2)!. The centered-potential pairwise variance identity and sign orthogonality give E||h_s||²=W(T)/n. Rademacher fourth-moment expansion yields E||h_s||⁴ <= 3(E||h_s||²)², proving universal bounds by Hölder. The star limit follows from a binomial signed sum; Donsker and bounded L² imply the Brownian path profile and convergence of mean area; the mean-zero Neumann covariance spectrum and Euler product give the exact constant. A separate finite checker computes actual facet Gram determinants and tree metric values over 360 signed facets and reproduces the exact identities and decimal. No finite experiment is substituted for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Canonical tree root polytopes all have exactly the crosspolytope combinatorial type and identical intrinsic Euclidean volume, making varying Euclidean boundary geometry natural to determine. The all-tree exact squared facet-area identity extracts the meaningful graph metric Wiener index from geometric data. The path facet area converges to a nondegenerate Brownian functional while star facets concentrate, and their total Euclidean surface areas separate by a sharp sqrt(n) ratio with a nontrivial integral constant. These structural distinctions go well beyond numerical facet tables, unmotivated slices or restatements of crosspolytope face counts.
